setup: 🐞 SCENARIO: sunbasker. Gold in the grass, three tiles east. It was not there, then it was.
log: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
📖 LEARNED: Star Navigation (Level 1). North Star is constant. Find the Big Dipper, follow the pointer stars. You always know north.
📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
📖 LEARNED: Radios & Signals (Level 1). Continuity, batteries, and solder. Most dead electronics are just broken connections.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 4 skills from your past — check your Journal.
Nothing here looks like home. You know none of these plants. Learn fast.
📖 Your hands remember: knap a Stone knife (stone + vine) — the oldest tool there is. Find the stone.
📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Ibrahim Diallo. Bush pilot. From Minneapolis, USA. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Photo album, Hard Candy, Trail compass, Unnamed photograph, Carpenter's square. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
A man, maybe 40s, with calloused knuckles: "Don't bother picking around the tents. Walk out. The land feeds people who go looking."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

Its scales are going gold. It's charging.
🦎 It moves.
Gold in the grass. It was not there, then it was — a lizard the size of a dog, tilting its back to the sun.
You don't know what that was. a gold flash in the grass, gone when you look Someone at the haven should hear about this.

Lizard the size of a dog. Tastes like chicken, if chicken sunbathed. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.
You clutch your Photo Album, Hard Candy, Trail compass, Unnamed photograph, Carpenter's square. You're still here.
